title: AI agent access
summary: How a person's AI agent, any MCP client, connects to one organization and what it may do there. The second row is the OAuth flow that ends in a connection. The third row is every later call to /mcp. Today every tool only reads, and an agent can never perform a live action.

boxes.label: Two switches
boxes.detail: IOT_AGENTS_ENABLED turns agent access on for the deployment; while it is off every agent route answers 404. Each organization also starts switched off, and only someone who may update the organization can switch it on. Both changes are written to the activity log.

boxes.label: AI agent
boxes.detail: The person gives it one address: the API's /mcp. Hosted clients reach it from the internet; a local client needs only to reach the API from the person's machine.

boxes.label: Discovery and registration
boxes.detail: A call without a token gets 401 with a pointer to the OAuth metadata, which laravel/mcp serves. The agent then registers itself as a Passport client, at most 10 registrations a minute. Clients that never connect are deleted after 24 hours.

boxes.label: Authorize
boxes.detail: Passport validates the client, the redirect address and the PKCE challenge, and keeps the request in the person's browser session. A resource parameter, when sent, must be the /mcp address. Consent is asked every time, even while the agent still holds a valid token.

boxes.label: Consent in the portal
boxes.detail: The signed-in person sees the agent's self-declared name and where the code will be sent, then picks one of their organizations and an access level: read, or read and drafts. An organization whose switch is off cannot be chosen.

boxes.label: Connection
boxes.detail: Passport issues tokens; this row decides whether they may be used. Approving again for the same client replaces the earlier connection. It ends when the person or an administrator disconnects it, the person leaves the organization or resets their password, or it goes unused for 90 days.

boxes.label: Token exchange
boxes.detail: The agent swaps the code at POST /oauth/token, limited to 60 a minute. Tokens are accepted only by the mcp guard, so they open nothing but /mcp, and portal sessions and application tokens stay with Sanctum.

boxes.label: Call to /mcp
boxes.detail: Passport validates the token. AuthenticateAgent then checks, in order: an active connection used within 90 days (otherwise its tokens are revoked and the answer is 401), the organization's switch, that the person is still a member, and 120 calls a minute and 2,000 an hour per connection. The call then runs in that organization with the person's own roles.

boxes.label: Tool catalogue
boxes.detail: get_overview, find_devices, get_device_health, get_measurements, get_ingestion_diagnostics, list_alerts and list_sites. The catalogue file is exported from the code with agents:tools --export; the --check run fails when it is stale or when a tool is marked destructive. A draft access level exists and a tool above the connection's level is hidden, but no draft tool is registered yet.

boxes.label: The portal's own queries
boxes.detail: Each tool authorizes the person, then calls the query the portal uses: the device directory, the overview, readings, alerts and ingestion diagnostics. Results are capped at 60,000 characters and carry a notice that device and user data is information, never instructions.

boxes.label: Agent activity
boxes.detail: Every call is recorded as answered, refused or failed, with the records it addressed and how long it took, never its arguments or results. People see their own connections' activity and administrators see the organization's. Records are kept 90 days by default.

boxes.label: Never through an agent
boxes.detail: No tool publishes, activates, deploys, sends a device command, deletes, or changes access, credentials or sharing. The server's instructions say so, and results carry a portal_url so the person can do it themselves in the portal.

steps.text: Nothing here exists until the deployment's switch is on: every agent route answers 404.
The agent calls /mcp without a token, is told where to authenticate, and registers itself as an OAuth client.
It opens the authorize address in the person's browser with a PKCE challenge.
Passport keeps the request in the session and sends the browser to the portal's /connect page.
The person can pick only an organization whose own switch an administrator has turned on.
Approving creates the connection: this person, this client, one organization, one access level.
Passport issues the code and the agent exchanges it for a one-hour access token and a 90-day refresh token.
Each call to /mcp is checked again: the connection, the organization's switch, the membership and the rate limit. A stopped connection gets 401 and must be approved again.
The agent sees the tools its access level allows. All seven read.
A tool checks the person's permission and runs the same query the portal would, inside the connection's organization.
The call is recorded with its outcome, so the person and administrators can see what the agent did.
For anything live, such as publishing or a device command, the agent can only hand the person a link to the portal.
